name: Seqora Order Numbers for WooCommerce
author: Vijendra Yadav

sections.description:
WooCommerce numbers orders using the underlying post or order ID, which jumps around as other content is created. This plugin gives every order a predictable, human friendly number instead.

Requires WooCommerce 5.0 or newer, and is tested up to WooCommerce 11.1.

Features

  • Sequential order numbers applied automatically to new orders.
  • Prefix and suffix, for example ORD-1001 or 1001-EU.
  • Date placeholders anywhere in the number, using any PHP date format.
  • Ready made format presets, plus a custom pattern field for full control.
  • Zero padded number length, so 1 becomes 0001.
  • Configurable start number, useful when migrating from another platform.
  • Custom increment, so numbers can step by 5, 10 or any interval.
  • Automatic counter reset on a daily, monthly or yearly cycle, with its own start number.
  • A separate sequence and format for free (zero total) orders.
  • Optional refund numbers derived from the parent order.
  • Renumber existing orders: all of them, everything from a date, or everything from an order ID, run in batches with a progress bar.
  • Search the admin order list by custom order number.
  • Customers can use the custom number in the order tracking form.
  • Works with WooCommerce Subscriptions, including renewal orders.
  • Compatible with High Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the block based checkout.
  • Tools to set a single order’s number by hand, reset the counters, or restore WooCommerce’s default numbering.

Placeholders

{prefix}, `{number}`, `{suffix}`, `{date}`, `{year}`, `{short_year}`, `{month}`, `{day}`, `{order_id}`, `{customer_id}`, and inline dates such as `{date:Y-m}`.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the seqora-order-numbers-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or upload the zip through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Order Numbers to configure the format.
sections.faq:
Will existing orders be renumbered?

Not unless you ask. The default scope is “Upcoming orders only”. Choose a wider scope on the Order number format tab, save, then run the job from the Tools tab.

Are the numbers safe under load?

Yes. Each number is allocated inside a MySQL named lock, so two simultaneous checkouts cannot receive the same value.

What happens to abandoned block checkout carts?

Draft orders are skipped, so numbers are not consumed by carts that were never completed.

Does it work with HPOS?

Yes. The plugin declares compatibility with High Performance Order Storage and reads and writes order meta through the active storage engine.
